Create one opaque square repeatable ground field for a modern Earth training-base game. Show a broad expanse of firm dry compacted soil with sparse embedded very fine crushed-mineral grit, viewed from a distant orthographic gameplay camera, not a close-up gravel photograph. Soil forms the continuous surface; tiny angular mineral grains are restrained, not a field of individual large pebbles. Fill the entire square with this same continuous material, no horizon or objects.

At normal gameplay size the first impression is a quiet muted warm grey-tan ground plane, with extremely fine crisp irregular structure and low-amplitude short-range variation. Most individual grains are unresolved or at most one logical display pixel; do not enlarge grains to demonstrate detail. At double display resolution subtle tiny mineral fragments and compact soil pores can remain legible. Uniform diffuse daylight, nondirectional surface appearance, no baked cast shadows or directional highlight pattern. Aim near warm muted sRGB(163,146,119), somewhat brighter than quiet olive lawn but distinctly earth-like and warmer/darker than pale engineered concrete. No orange desert sand or yellow sparkle.

Think of the distant view of a broad roughly ten-metre-square maintained utility ground field, not a literal scale conversion or a tiny material swatch. This whole image maps to384x384 logical gameplay pixels,768x768 at density2. The entire square must form one repeatable field, opposite edges and all corners joining naturally, with no noticeable repeated clouds, border or gradient.

No paths, trails, tire ruts, footprints, painted markings, vegetation, grass patches, large stones, rounded decorative pebbles, boulders, stone clusters, cracks, dark holes, raised ridges, terrain slopes, paving, tiles, shadows, buildings, props, text or labels. No blur or uniform digital noise; use crisp very fine natural surface detail with restrained contrast. Return one completely opaque square image of only this broad flat ground material.
